items.q: Why does ThePrimeagen call frontier-model gating "security theater"?
items.a: He argues **gated access** to cybersecurity models achieves **control, not security**. Anthropic's Mythos/Fable path — broad release, government pullback, then **critical-infrastructure-only** — is a **Project Glass Wing** replay. OpenAI's GPT 5.6 "trusted partners" preview fits the same pattern.

items.q: What does "Daddy Dario" mean in this critique?
items.a: Primeagen reads Dario Amodei's logic as: **control the inputs → control the outputs**. Monitor usage, slow rollout, and regulation sound like safety but function as **gatekeeping** that doesn't stop the open-weight scaling Dario warned about in 2023.

items.q: Do closed frontier models actually lead on security benchmarks?
items.a: On Sam Gre's **IDOR** benchmark, **GLM 5.2 with no harness** scores **39%**, beating **Claude Opus 4.8 at 28–37% with Claude Code harness** and GPT 5.5/Codex around **~20%**. Much of coding-agent gain is **harness/tooling**, not weights alone.

items.q: How affordable is offensive open-weight capability?
items.a: Bad actors can **download from Hugging Face** and rent cloud GPUs at roughly **$73/hour**, then run offline. Scam economics can exceed that hourly cost. **Hermes** (GPT 5.5 + Opus 4.8) and Microsoft multi-agent stacks even score **above Mythos** on the same tests.

items.q: How does selective access make the world less safe?
items.a: Restricting defenders while attackers retain capability creates a **defender access deficit**. Offensive teams get in via **insider leaks** or equally capable **open models**; ordinary developers and OSS maintainers lag. Federation and lockstep patching beat selective "good guy" lists.

items.q: Why does IDOR matter as the benchmark choice?
items.a: **Insecure direct object reference** — pass an arbitrary user ID and leak data — is **HackerOne's #4** real-world vuln class. Benchmarking on IDOR ties model scores to a vulnerability defenders actually fight every day.

items.q: What access policy does Michael Arnaldi argue for?
items.a: **No guardrails**, immediate widest release of the strongest models, and **free usage for core infrastructure maintainers**. Paraphrased: **"The only thing you achieve by restricting access is unsafety 100%."** Restriction guarantees offensive advantage over maintainers securing software.
